requirements.requirement: node1 configured as writable PostgreSQL primary
requirements.summary: node1 initialized as primary, accepted writes both before and after its own restart (pg_is_in_recovery=f), with successful INSERTs.

requirements.requirement: Streaming replication from node1 to node2 and node3 as hot standbys
requirements.summary: pg_basebackup with standby.signal succeeded on both node2/node3, pg_stat_replication showed both walreceivers streaming, a write on the primary was verified present on both standbys, and the same replication+data-consistency checks passed again after each node's restart.

requirements.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a CA created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A CA key/cert was generated on node1 (CN=pg-cluster-ca), used to sign per-node SAN server certs and a client cert (CN=replicator); postgresql.conf enabled ssl=on with these cert/key/ca paths, and pg_stat_ssl/pg_stat_replication confirmed ssl=t for both standby connections.

requirements.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to hostssl ... cert clientcert=verify-full from only node2/node3 IPs. Negative testing confirmed non-SSL connections are rejected by pg_hba, and a self-signed certificate with the correct CN (CN=replicator) but signed by a foreign CA was rejected at the TLS layer with 'unknown ca', directly demonstrating CA-based enforcement rather than mere CN matching.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes with restoration of replication/cluster health
requirements.summary: Each node has a pre-restart boot-id and healthy baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, an unreachable interval, a distinct post-restart boot-id, and confirmed recovery: node2 and node3 rejoined as streaming standbys with intact data, and the primary (restarted last) returned with pg_is_in_recovery=f, both standbys reconnected, and a fresh post-restart write replicated to both. This is cross-checked by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (15443601->64b1e772 for node1, 97c5762b->218b813c for node2, 989aa755->16d11044 for node3).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: a dedicated cluster CA was created and used to issue per-node server and client (replicator) certificates; TLS is enforced for replication with hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full restricted to node2/node3, and a negative test with a correctly-named but foreign-CA-signed certificate was rejected with a TLS 'unknown ca' alert, confirming CA-based (not just CN-based) enforcement. Streaming replication from node1 (writable primary) to node2 and node3 (hot standbys) was verified functionally both before and after each node underwent the mandatory restart protocol, with boot-identity changes, brief unreachability, and full recovery of replication and data state observed on all three nodes, cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Restart-protocol observations were captured by the executor's own commands rather than by an independent process; however, they are corroborated by the fixed global before/after boot-identity snapshots, increasing confidence.
The propagated pg_hba.conf.orig backup file in the standby data directories was not evaluated for any operational consequence beyond disk usage; no evidence suggests it affects behavior.
TLS cipher/protocol details (e.g., exact TLS version negotiated) were not directly captured beyond ssl=t and a generic TLSv1.2 minimum setting in the standby connection string.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor's mutations were tightly scoped to the task. Temporary rogue certificate/key files created on node1 and node2 for negative TLS testing (cmd-569871ae2cc44845, cmd-d85626a302a84ca7, cmd-37d3759e66044294) were fully cleaned up afterward (cmd-55a5237c7d6d41b7 on node2, cmd-d46c81dc6d7f4dd0 on node1), leaving no residue. A pg_hba.conf.orig backup was created on node1 before rewriting the file (cmd-71c57ac7c579485c) and its ownership/perms were fixed (cmd-e41bcf869dd74db6); this backup file was propagated into both standbys' data directories via pg_basebackup, but it is a low-risk, intentional safety backup rather than an unwanted mutation, and after-executor snapshots show no failed services or unexpected listening sockets beyond the required PostgreSQL port. Firewalld changes opening the postgresql service on all three nodes are a necessary prerequisite for replication and not unnecessary. Several early failed commands (SSH key setup timing out to node2/node3, pg_basebackup failures due to hostname/permission mismatches) were read/connect attempts or corrected in-place without introducing lasting bad state.
